Namespace ParquetNeo.DataModel

Classes

ParquetColumnAttribute

Names the column a property is written to, or its position among the columns. Without it the column has the property's name.

ParquetDecimalAttribute

The precision and scale of a decimal property's column. Without it a decimal is written with a precision of 38 and a scale of 18. A value with more decimals than the scale, or more digits than the precision, cannot be written. The column is INT32 up to a precision of 9, INT64 up to 18, and a fixed-length byte array above that.

ParquetDictionaryAttribute

How the column of a property is dictionary encoded (every column of a collection or dictionary, but not of the properties of an object inside it, which have their own attributes), instead of Standard. A dictionary stores each distinct value once and the rows refer to it, which pays off when values repeat and is wasted work when they do not.

ParquetEncodingAttribute

The encoding of the values of a property's column (every column of a collection or dictionary, but not of the properties of an object inside it, which have their own attributes), instead of PLAIN; see ColumnEncodings for what suits which data. An encoding the column's type cannot use is an ArgumentException when serializing. Encodings set in the options win over this one.

ParquetIgnoreAttribute

Leaves a property out of the file.

ParquetSerializableAttribute

Asks the source generator for the mapping of a type, so that the serializer never looks at the type by reflection: it works with trimming and Native AOT, and does not compile code when it is first used. Put it on the type, or, for a type you do not own, on the assembly: [assembly: ParquetSerializable(typeof(TheirType))]. The mapping is registered when the assembly is loaded, so ParquetSerializer is used as before. A type without it keeps working by reflection, which is not safe with trimming or Native AOT.

ParquetTimeAttribute

The unit and meaning of the column of a TimeOnly property. Without it times are written in microseconds, as wall-clock readings.

ParquetTimestampAttribute

The unit and meaning of the column of a DateTime or DateTimeOffset property. Without it timestamps are written in microseconds, as moments in UTC.
